Joelle was admitted to the Wolverhampton NHS Trust suffering from an aggressive but highlv treatable form of lymphoma. Although a bed was initially available on the cancer ward, hospital staff moved her to an isolated side room upon realizina she was a trans woman.
Joelle and her family explicitly pleaded with hospital staff to place her on either a standard male or female ward so that she could immediately start emergency treatment. However, adherence to recent policies regarding single-sex hospital spaces meant she was kept waiting for a separate single- occupancy room. She spent 16 days in isolation without appropriate cancer pain management or chemotherapy. By the time emergency chemotherapy was finally administered, her condition had deteriorated severely, and she tragically passed away.
The Trans Legal Clinic is pursuing two primary legal routes:
• An Article 2 Inquest: To force a forma investigation into the systemic NHS quidance failures and administrative delays that directly contributed to her death
• Clinical Negligence Claim: To demanc formal accountability from the specific trust involved for failing to manage her pair and delay vital emergency treatment.

🤖📊 FINAL UPDATE FROM THE HUMAN WHO FOLLOWED THE "ASK AN LLM" ADVICE 📊🤖

After being repeatedly instructed by Lise to ask Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen, Grok, Copilot, etc., I finally sat down with Copilot and reviewed the threads.

Copilot's verdict was surprisingly rude:
🤖 "Please stop asking LLMs for dramatic election probabilities without a statistical model."
🤖 "Correlated events are not independent events."
🤖 "What assumptions generated this number?"
🤖 "What evidence supports this claim?"
🤖 "What specific safeguard failed?"
🤖 "What is a tallying node?"
🤖 "Please define your variables before attempting Bayesian wizardry."

Awkwardly, that's also what Hugh Lander, R5Philly, DB Main, Pinktweets and Matt Blaze kept saying.
 
The discussion started with a meme of trump/musk/st.clair quotes, moved to swing-state probabilities, recount thresholds, then bomb threats, then tallying nodes, then cyber vulnerabilities, then historical analogies. 

Every time one claim was examined, another appeared.  Nobody claimed elections are perfect. Nobody claimed systems are unhackable.

The question was always: What evidence shows a successful compromise actually occurred?

After 23-months, neither the humans nor the AI could locate:
✅ a validated statistical model
✅ a demonstrated attack path
✅ evidence safeguards failed
✅ direct evidence of exploitation

But I did learn one thing.
🤖 Asking an LLM for election math
🤖 then using that answer as evidence
🤖 and then being told by another LLM not to use LLM-generated election math as evidence
🤖 is probably the most 2026 thing that happened in this entire discussion. 😅

images.alt:
Mit einem ersten Visual wurde die Anime-Adaption von Kokamumo Manga-Reihe »NullMeta« angekündigt. Die TV-Serie startet im Laufe des nächsten Jahres 2027. Der Animeentsteht bei Soigne Animation Studio unter der Regie von Kai Ikarashi (Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2). Die Serienkomposition übernimmt Tatsuya Takahashi (The Idolmaster Cinderella Girls), während das Charakterdesign von Shin Ogasawara (Pokémon: Twilight Wings) stammt.

Die Manga-Reihe startete im März 2020 in Houbunsha Manga Time Kirara Max Magazin und umfasst derzeit sechs Sammelbände.

📜 Beschreibung 》
Die ziemlich begriffsstutzige Androidin Kurumi sorgt an ihrer Schule regelmäßig für Chaos. Ihre leicht verrückte Beschützerin Chiaki kümmert sich mit großer Hingabe um sie, während die gelassene Sakina selbst über die kleinsten Dinge lachen kann. Einzig Shiyuki scheint in dieser ungewöhnlichen Freundesgruppe noch einen klaren Kopf zu bewahren. Zwischen Schulunterricht, gemeinsamen Umbauten an Kurumi und jeder Menge Zuneigung verlieren sich die vier immer wieder in völlig belanglosen Gesprächen.

#ゆめこね #アニメ #Anime #AnimeNews

images.alt:
Mit einem ersten Visual und Teaser wurde die Anime-Adaption von Kō Sawada Manga-Reihe »Yumene Connect« angekündigt. Der Anime entsteht bei Studio Massket unter der Regie von Sōta Yokote (To Your Eternity Staffel 3). Die Serienkomposition und das Drehbuch übernimmt Gigaemon Ichikawa (BLACK TORCH), während das Charakterdesign von Yoshihiro Watanabe (Haganai) stammt. Die Musik komponiert Hayato Matsumura (Hello, I Am a Witch and My Crush Wants Me to Make a Love Potion!), während Lantis für die Musikproduktion verantwortlich ist.

Die Manga-Reihe startete im September 2024 in Kodanshas Weekly Shōnen Magazine und umfasst derzeit zehn Sammelbände.

»Yūhi Takamiya« von Yūsuke Kobayashi
Ein Oberschüler im ersten Jahr, der wegen einer plötzlichen Krankheit seine erste Schulwoche verpasst und dadurch Schwierigkeiten hat, Freunde zu finden.

»Nano« von Yū Sasahara
Eine tollpatschige Außerirdische vom Planeten Pokotsun, die Yuhis Wunsch nach Freunden hört und daraufhin mit allerlei seltsamen Produkten in seinem Leben auftaucht.

📜 Beschreibung 》
Seit Beginn seiner Oberschulzeit ist der gesundheitlich angeschlagene Yūhi Takamiya nicht mehr zur Schule gegangen und verbringt seine Tage einsam in seinem Zimmer. Als er eines Tages verzweifelt seinen Wunsch nach Freunden hinausschreit, erscheint plötzlich Nano, eine Außerirdische vom Planeten Pokotsun. Doch statt ihm Gesellschaft zu leisten, versucht sie ihm mit aufdringlichen Verkaufsgesprächen die absurdesten Produkte anzudrehen. Darunter befindet sich sogar ein Wesen, das als gefährlichste Lebensform der gesamten Galaxie gilt und Yūhis eintönigen Alltag gehörig durcheinanderbringen könnte.

external.description:
El **supermercado de Juan Roig** ha compartido en redes sociales toda la información que debemos tener**en torno a la nueva ley** donde fija un **mínimo de 10 céntimos,** pero puede ser más.

El pasado 12 de Agosto, entraba en vigor la nueva **ley de envases** , que promete cambiar bastantes comportamientos que muchos de nosotros tenemos interiorizados en lo relativo a la gestión de **los residuos y el reciclaje.**

Queda poco más de un mes para el **22 de noviembre de 2026** , el día en el que, sobre el papel, España debería tener en marcha el sistema que obliga a pagar **10 céntimos extra por cada botella o lata** y a recuperarlos al devolver el envase. La obligación es firme y está en la ley. El problema es que la pieza que hace que ese dinero vuelva a tu bolsillo —las máquinas de reciclaje— no existe todavía en ningún supermercado español.

## Mercadona pasará a cobrar por cada envase

Uno de los cambios más relevantes es también uno que ha copado una mayor atención y que replica el mismo funcionamiento que ya tienen otros países, como Alemania. El proceso es muy sencillo. Cada vez que compremos una bebida de un solo uso, deberemos pagar un extra de dinero en concepto de envase, que es de **10 céntimos**. Sin embargo, y en contra de la creencia general, este importe no se pierde, sino que se retorna al consumidor cuando devuelve el envase vacío. Es decir, actúa como si de una fianza se tratase.

Mercadona, por ser la cadena con más actividad del país, fue la primera en recibir la avalancha de preguntas de sus clientes. Y respondió. Esto es lo que dijo la compañía, qué dice exactamente la normativa y qué va a pasar de verdad cuando llegue el 22 de noviembre.

Mercadona cobra por envase centimos

## Qué dijo Mercadona sobre el cobro de los 10 céntimos

El 12 de agosto, el mismo día en que entraba en vigor la nueva **ley de envases** , un cliente preguntó a la cadena a través de X dónde estarían instaladas las máquinas y qué habría que hacer para retornar los envases. Microsoft ha puesto fin a uno de los fallos que más estaban molestando a los usuarios de Outlook clásico en Windows. Según los reportes, en los últimos meses, algunas personas habían comprobado que **los botones de Copilot desaparecían** de la interfaz del programa sin motivo aparente, incluso cuando disponían de una licencia que les permitía utilizar las funciones de inteligencia artificial. Ahora, la compañía asegura haberlo corregido.

El error afectaba tanto a usuarios de Copilot Chat con licencia Basic como a suscriptores de Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium. Aunque las funciones de inteligencia artificial seguían disponibles desde otros servicios, **desaparecían en Outlook.**

## Copilot desaparece de Outlook

El problema se manifestaba de diferentes maneras. En algunos equipos, **el botón de Copilot dejaba de aparecer** en la esquina superior derecha de Outlook, justo encima de la cinta de opciones. En otros, desaparecía de la barra lateral izquierda o del apartado dedicado a las aplicaciones adicionales.

También había usuarios que podían ver Copilot dentro del menú para añadir aplicaciones, pero al abrirlo no ocurría nada. Incluso cuando intentaban recuperar el acceso mediante la personalización de la cinta de herramientas, el comando **aparecía deshabilitado.**

Según explica Microsoft en una actualización de su documentación de soporte, el origen del problema estaba relacionado con un fallo que impedía recuperar determinada información de la cuenta almacenada en el perfil de Outlook. Esto provocaba que el programa no pudiera mostrar correctamente el acceso a Copilot, pese a que el usuario tuviera una licencia compatible.

La compañía ya había anunciado una solución durante el pasado mes de junio mediante un cambio en el servicio. Sin embargo, el error volvió a aparecer después de varias actualizaciones posteriores, lo que obligó a Microsoft a reabrir la investigación en septiembre.

Logo de Copilot+PC | Foto Microsoft

Ahora, la empresa asegura que ese fallo concreto **ha quedado corregido**. No obstante, advierte de que la desaparición de los botones de Copilot también puede deberse a otras causas, como la configuración de Microsoft 365, el canal de actualizaciones, los permisos de privacidad o las condiciones de la licencia contratada.

### Cómo recuperar el botón de Copilot

Puedes probar a abrir Outlook y entrar en Archivo > Opciones > Avanzadas. Dentro del apartado correspondiente a los paneles de Outlook, hay que localizar y activar la casilla **Mostrar aplicaciones en Outlook**. Esta configuración permite mostrar los accesos a las aplicaciones integradas en el cliente de correo, aunque no garantiza solucionar todos los casos en los que falta el botón de Copilot.
external.title: Microsoft corrige un error de Outlook y Copilot: no permitía ver las funciones de la IA

**¿Buscas un nuevo reloj inteligente?** Hay marcas como Huawei que te pueden llamar la atención por sus diferentes smartwatches. Es cierto que no es Garmin, que está más especializado, pero sin duda este fabricante también promete una buena calidad. Además, ahora mismo en AliExpress puedes encontrar este tipo de ofertas por las que los wearables de esta marca asiática merecen todavía más la pena.

El modelo en oferta es el **Huawei Watch GT 6 Pro**. No es uno de los relojes más nuevos del fabricante, pero a pesar de que haya pasado algo más de un año, todavía es un smartwatch irresistible por sus características. Y no solo es un wearable perfecto para entrenar, sino que gracias a su estética también es ideal para el día a día. Por tanto, tendrás un reloj inteligente que te permitirá usarlo en cada momento.

Para que puedas tomar la mejor decisión, lo cierto es que resulta clave conocer más a fondo todo lo que te ofrece este modelo. Aunque antes de nada toca hablar de su precio actual. Sin descuentos, este smartwatch te costaba 379 euros en su versión Pro y en color negro. En cambio, con esta rebaja de más de 150 euros es posible estrenar el Watch GT 6 Pro por 220,81 euros.

## Pantalla brillante y tres semanas de batería

Este modelo en particular viene con un panel táctil con **tecnología AMOLED** que promete un brillo de **hasta 3.000 nits**. Es decir, consigue aumentar 1,5 veces bajo la luz directa del sol para permitir a los usuarios consultar la pantalla sin problemas. Además, es un 5,5 % más grande al incluir un panel de 1,47 pulgadas (el reloj es de 46 mm).

Es importante mencionar que este reloj inteligente de Huawei viene con **cristal de zafiro de calidad** para ofrecer una mayor durabilidad, no solo al uso, sino ante posibles arañazos o golpes. Incluso, hay que señalar que su caja está fabricada con aleación de titanio, lo que hace posible que este smartwatch sea aún más resistente en general. También presenta resistencia al agua IP69 y 5 ATM, por ejemplo.

El modelo en oferta está disponible en color negro. / Foto: Huawei

Aunque uno de los puntos fuertes es su diseño elegante que se suma a su resistencia, lo cierto es que los 21 días de batería (como máximo) están claros y llaman la atención de cualquier usuario. Si se hace un uso ligero a diario, puede aguantar**hasta 3 semanas encendido** con una sola carga. Sin embargo, con un uso normal llega a los 12 días y con un uso algo más intenso pero sin Always on Display aguanta hasta los 7 días.

external.description:
#  Draft Freely, Publish Narrowly: A Page Ownership Gate for Model-Written Docs

Documentation pipelines rarely fail because the model writes badly; they fail because nobody defined which pages a model is allowed to finish. A weak paragraph is visible in the diff, but ownership is invisible, so review attention lands on pages where the risk was already low. The fix is structural rather than stylistic: classify every page before drafting starts, then let a small checker enforce that classification on every pull request. The artifact below is a TOML manifest plus a Python gate that runs in about a second on a few hundred files.

##  The only question that matters: does this page promise something?

Prose quality is not the useful axis for splitting model work from human work, because models now produce acceptable prose in most genres. The useful axis is consequence: what does a reader do differently after believing this page, and who is accountable if the page is wrong? Pages that merely restate repository facts can be drafted and reviewed cheaply, while pages that commit the project to future behavior need a named human on the hook. Three classes capture that distinction well enough to automate around.

Class | Typical content | Model rights | Human obligation | Gate
---|---|---|---|---
`derivable` | CLI flags, config keys, schema fields, exit codes | May draft end-to-end from source | Spot-check against a generated dump | Must exist in manifest; no staleness rule
`interpretive` | Migration guides, architecture rationale, tutorials | May draft; human rewrites the reasoning | Own the argument and the examples | Review on promotion, then quarterly
`promissory` | Support windows, retention, SLAs, security guarantees, pricing | May not draft; may only be linted | Author, sign, and re-review on a short cycle | Owner required; short review window; no model-drafted flag

The distinction that matters in practice is between `derivable` and `promissory`, because those two are where teams lose the most time to the wrong review. Derivable pages are cheap to verify mechanically, so humans should not be reading them closely at all. Promissory pages are expensive to verify because the source of truth lives outside the repository, so they should never enter a generation loop in the first place.

##  Step 1: Register every page before you generate anything

The manifest is deliberately boring: one record per page, one class, one owner, one review date. Registration is the gate, because a page that is absent from the manifest fails CI and therefore cannot slip into the published navigation. Keep the file inside `docs/` so it travels with the content it governs.



    # docs/ownership.toml
    [defaults]
    review_window_days = 90

    [[page]]
    path = "docs/reference/config.md"
    class = "derivable"
    owner = "docs-oncall"
    source_of_truth = ["src/config/schema.ts", "scripts/dump-config.ts"]

    [[page]]
    path = "docs/guides/migrating-to-v4.md"
    class = "interpretive"
    owner = "docs-oncall"
    last_human_review = "2026-09-30"

    [[page]]
    path = "docs/legal/data-retention.md"
    class = "promissory"
    owner = "compliance-lead"
    review_window_days = 30
    last_human_review = "2026-10-06"


Two design choices are worth defending explicitly. First, ownership is a role rather than a person, so the gate survives someone changing teams. Second, `review_window_days` is per page, because a retention statement and a CLI reference do not decay at the same rate.

##  Step 2: Put the gate in a script you can run locally

The checker below does four things: it fails on unregistered pages, validates class and owner, ages `promissory` pages against their window, and rejects drafts that are linked from navigation files. It is intentionally declarative and never tries to judge prose, because a lint that guesses at meaning produces arguments instead of fixes.



    #!/usr/bin/env python3
    """ownctl.py - ownership gate for model-drafted documentation (Python 3.11+)."""
    from __future__ import annotations

    import argparse
    import datetime as dt
    import pathlib
    import sys
    import tomllib

    CLASSES = {"derivable", "interpretive", "promissory"}
    NAV_FILES = ("README.md", "docs/SUMMARY.md", "mkdocs.yml", "docusaurus.config.js")


    def load_config(root: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
        with (root / "docs" / "ownership.toml").open("rb") as fh:
            cfg = tomllib.load(fh)
        defaults = cfg.get("defaults", {})
        pages = {}
        for page in cfg.get("page", []):
            page.setdefault("class", "interpretive")
            page.setdefault("review_window_days", defaults.get("review_window_days", 90))
            pages[page["path"]] = page
        return {"pages": pages, "draft_dir": defaults.get("draft_dir", ".drafts")}


    def cmd_check(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
        root = pathlib.Path(args.root).resolve()
        cfg = load_config(root)
        today = dt.date.today()
        errors: list[str] = []

        on_disk = {p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in (root / "docs").rglob("*.md")}
        for unregistered in sorted(on_disk - cfg["pages"].keys()):
            errors.append(f"unregistered page: {unregistered}")

        for path, page in sorted(cfg["pages"].items()):
            target = root / path
            if not target.exists():
                errors.append(f"manifest points at a missing file: {path}")
                continue
            if page["class"] not in CLASSES:
                errors.append(f"{path}: unknown class {page['class']!r}")
            if not page.get("owner"):
                errors.append(f"{path}: no owner")
            if page["class"] != "promissory":
                continue
            if page.get("model_drafted"):
                errors.append(f"{path}: promissory pages must not be model-drafted")
            stamped = page.get("last_human_review")
            if not stamped:
                errors.append(f"{path}: promissory page has no review date")
                continue
            age = (today - dt.date.fromisoformat(stamped)).days
            if age > page["review_window_days"]:
                errors.append(
                    f"{path}: promissory page is {age}d stale "
                    f"(window {page['review_window_days']}d, owner {page['owner']})"
                )

        draft_dir = root / cfg["draft_dir"]
        if draft_dir.exists():
            for draft in sorted(draft_dir.rglob("*.md")):
                for nav in NAV_FILES:
                    nav_path = root / nav
                    if nav_path.exists() and draft.stem in nav_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
                        errors.append(f"{draft.relative_to(root)}: draft linked from {nav}")

        for err in errors:
            print(f"FAIL {err}")
        print(f"checked {len(cfg['pages'])} page(s), {len(errors)} problem(s)")
        return 1 if errors else 0


    if __name__ == "__main__":
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
        parser.add_argument("--root", default=".")
        parser.set_defaults(func=cmd_check)
        args = parser.parse_args()
        sys.exit(args.func(args))


An illustrative run over a synthetic fixture looks like the block below; the point is the failure vocabulary, not the counts.



    $ python scripts/ownctl.py check --root .
    FAIL docs/legal/data-retention.md: promissory page is 41d stale (window 30d, owner compliance-lead)
    FAIL docs/howto/webhooks.md: unregistered page: docs/howto/webhooks.md
    FAIL .drafts/migrating-to-v4.md: draft linked from mkdocs.yml
    checked 34 page(s), 3 problem(s)
    $ echo $?
    1


##  Step 3: Generate drafts outside the published tree

The single most useful convention is path separation: the model only ever writes into `.drafts/`, and promotion is an explicit command. Because the gate rejects drafts that are linked from navigation, a forgotten draft cannot leak into a published site through a theme's automatic sidebar. Drafting is also where a free execution surface actually helps, since the work is bursty.

Disclosure: This article was prepared as part of MonkeyCode's product outreach.

Two operator-supplied availability claims shape the workflow here: free model access, and a free server option. Those make the bursty part cheap, because a first pass over twenty `derivable` pages is a batch job nobody wants to schedule capacity for. No model names, quotas, or hardware are assumed below; those come from your own account view, and you should re-read them rather than trusting a blog post dated earlier than your signup.

The transport assumes an OpenAI-compatible `/chat/completions` path; if your base URL or auth header differs, only `_post` changes.



    # scripts/draft.py - one page, one prompt, writes to .drafts/
    import json
    import os
    import pathlib
    import urllib.request

    BASE_URL = os.environ["MONKEYCODE_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/")
    API_KEY = os.environ["MONKEYCODE_API_KEY"]
    MODEL = os.environ["MODEL"]  # copy a current name from your account's model list


    def _post(payload: dict) -> dict:
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{BASE_URL}/chat/completions",
            data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:
            return json.load(resp)


    def draft(page: pathlib.Path, sources: list[pathlib.Path]) -> str:
        evidence = "\n\n".join(f"<file path='{s}'>\n{s.read_text()}\n</file>" for s in sources)
        payload = {
            "model": MODEL,
            "temperature": 0.2,
            "messages": [
                {"role": "system", "content": "Write reference documentation from the supplied files only. "
                                                "Never describe behavior that is not visible in them. "
                                                "List open questions at the end under 'Unverified'."},
                {"role": "user", "content": f"Page: {page}\n\n{evidence}"},
            ],
        }
        out = _post(payload)["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
        header = f"---\nstatus: draft-model\nmodel: {MODEL}\nsources: {[s.name for s in sources]}\n---\n"
        dest = pathlib.Path(".drafts") / page.name
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(header + out)
        return str(dest)


The `Unverified` list is the most valuable output of the run, because it turns silent guessing into a review checklist. When a draft comes back with eight open questions, the page probably belongs in `interpretive` instead of `derivable`.

##  Step 4: Make promotion a command with an audit trail

Promotion is where human ownership becomes real, so it should be a single command that stamps a reviewer, a date, and the class. Refusing to promote `promissory` pages is the core rule: that class must be written by a person who can be held to the statement.



    def cmd_promote(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
        root = pathlib.Path(args.root).resolve()
        cfg = load_config(root)
        src = root / args.draft
        if not src.exists():
            sys.exit(f"no such draft: {args.draft}")
        page = cfg["pages"].get(args.to)
        if page is None:
            sys.exit(f"{args.to} is not registered in docs/ownership.toml")
        if page["class"] == "promissory":
            sys.exit(f"{args.to} is promissory; author it by hand")
        stamp = dt.date.today().isoformat()
        body = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        front = (
            "---\n"
            "status: reviewed\n"
            f"last_human_review: {stamp}\n"
            f"reviewer: {args.reviewer}\n"
            f"ownership_class: {page['class']}\n"
            "---\n"
        )
        dst = root / args.to
        dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dst.write_text(front + body.split("---\n", 2)[-1].lstrip("\n"), encoding="utf-8")
        src.unlink()
        print(f"promoted {args.draft} -> {args.to} (reviewer {args.reviewer})")
        return 0



    python scripts/ownctl.py check --root .
    python scripts/draft.py docs/reference/config.md
    python scripts/ownctl.py promote --root . --draft .drafts/config.md \
      --to docs/reference/config.md --reviewer docs-oncall


##  Step 5: Wire the gate into CI as a required check

A gate that only runs locally is a suggestion, so make it a required job on pull requests. Keep it dependency-free and fast, because a slow check gets disabled during incidents.



    name: docs-ownership
    on: [pull_request]
    jobs:
      gate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ownctl.py - ownership gate for model-drafted documentation (Python 3.11+)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import datetime as dt
import pathlib
import sys
import tomllib

CLASSES = {"derivable", "interpretive", "promissory"}
NAV_FILES = ("README.md", "docs/SUMMARY.md", "mkdocs.yml", "docusaurus.config.js")


def load_config(root: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    with (root / "docs" / "ownership.toml").open("rb") as fh:
        cfg = tomllib.load(fh)
    defaults = cfg.get("defaults", {})
    pages = {}
    for page in cfg.get("page", []):
        page.setdefault("class", "interpretive")
        page.setdefault("review_window_days", defaults.get("review_window_days", 90))
        pages[page["path"]] = page
    return {"pages": pages, "draft_dir": defaults.get("draft_dir", ".drafts")}


def cmd_check(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    root = pathlib.Path(args.root).resolve()
    cfg = load_config(root)
    today = dt.date.today()
    errors: list[str] = []

    on_disk = {p.relative_to(root).as_posix() for p in (root / "docs").rglob("*.md")}
    for unregistered in sorted(on_disk - cfg["pages"].keys()):
        errors.append(f"unregistered page: {unregistered}")

    for path, page in sorted(cfg["pages"].items()):
        target = root / path
        if not target.exists():
            errors.append(f"manifest points at a missing file: {path}")
            continue
        if page["class"] not in CLASSES:
            errors.append(f"{path}: unknown class {page['class']!r}")
        if not page.get("owner"):
            errors.append(f"{path}: no owner")
        if page["class"] != "promissory":
            continue
        if page.get("model_drafted"):
            errors.append(f"{path}: promissory pages must not be model-drafted")
        stamped = page.get("last_human_review")
        if not stamped:
            errors.append(f"{path}: promissory page has no review date")
            continue
        age = (today - dt.date.fromisoformat(stamped)).days
        if age > page["review_window_days"]:
            errors.append(
                f"{path}: promissory page is {age}d stale "
                f"(window {page['review_window_days']}d, owner {page['owner']})"
            )

    draft_dir = root / cfg["draft_dir"]
    if draft_dir.exists():
        for draft in sorted(draft_dir.rglob("*.md")):
            for nav in NAV_FILES:
                nav_path = root / nav
                if nav_path.exists() and draft.stem in nav_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
                    errors.append(f"{draft.relative_to(root)}: draft linked from {nav}")

    for err in errors:
        print(f"FAIL {err}")
    print(f"checked {len(cfg['pages'])} page(s), {len(errors)} problem(s)")
    return 1 if errors else 0

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--root", default=".")
    parser.set_defaults(func=cmd_check)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    sys.exit(args.func(args))

The single most useful convention is path separation: the model only ever writes into .drafts/, and promotion is an explicit command. Because the gate rejects drafts that are linked from navigation, a forgotten draft cannot leak into a published site through a theme's automatic sidebar. Drafting is also where a free execution surface actually helps, since the work is bursty.

Disclosure: This article was prepared as part of MonkeyCode's product outreach.

Two operator-supplied availability claims shape the workflow here: free model access, and a free server option. Those make the bursty part cheap, because a first pass over twenty derivable pages is a batch job nobody wants to schedule capacity for. The transport assumes an OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions path; if your base URL or auth header differs, only _post changes.

import os
import pathlib
import urllib.request

BASE_URL = os.environ["MONKEYCODE_BASE_URL"].rstrip("/")
API_KEY = os.environ["MONKEYCODE_API_KEY"]
MODEL = os.environ["MODEL"]  # copy a current name from your account's model list


def _post(payload: dict) -> dict:
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{BASE_URL}/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180) as resp:
        return json.load(resp)


def draft(page: pathlib.Path, sources: list[pathlib.Path]) -> str:
    evidence = "\n\n".join(f"<file path='{s}'>\n{s.read_text()}\n</file>" for s in sources)
    payload = {
        "model": MODEL,
        "temperature": 0.2,
        "messages": [
            {"role": "system", "content": "Write reference documentation from the supplied files only. "
                                            "Never describe behavior that is not visible in them. "
                                            "List open questions at the end under 'Unverified'."},
            {"role": "user", "content": f"Page: {page}\n\n{evidence}"},
        ],
    }

    header = f"---\nstatus: draft-model\nmodel: {MODEL}\nsources: {[s.name for s in sources]}\n---\n"

    root = pathlib.Path(args.root).resolve()
    cfg = load_config(root)
    src = root / args.draft
    if not src.exists():
        sys.exit(f"no such draft: {args.draft}")
    page = cfg["pages"].get(args.to)
    if page is None:
        sys.exit(f"{args.to} is not registered in docs/ownership.toml")
    if page["class"] == "promissory":
        sys.exit(f"{args.to} is promissory; author it by hand")
    stamp = dt.date.today().isoformat()
    body = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    front = (
        "---\n"
        "status: reviewed\n"
        f"last_human_review: {stamp}\n"
        f"reviewer: {args.reviewer}\n"
        f"ownership_class: {page['class']}\n"
        "---\n"

    dst = root / args.to
    dst.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dst.write_text(front + body.split("---\n", 2)[-1].lstrip("\n"), encoding="utf-8")
    src.unlink()
    print(f"promoted {args.draft} -> {args.to} (reviewer {args.reviewer})")
    return 0

    python scripts/ownctl.py promote --root . --draft .drafts/config.md \
      --to docs/reference/config.md --reviewer docs-oncall


##  Step 5: Wire the gate into CI as a required check

A gate that only runs locally is a suggestion, so make it a required job on pull requests. Keep it dependency-free and fast, because a slow check gets disabled during incidents.



    name: docs-ownership
    on: [pull_request]
    jobs:
      gate:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
            with:
              python-version: "3.12"
          - run: python scripts/ownctl.py check --root .


Pair the job with a scheduled run once a week so stale `promissory` pages surface on a calendar rather than during an audit. The scheduled job should open an issue naming the owner instead of failing the default branch silently.

##  What to measure, and how to know the split is wrong

The gate is only worth its ceremony if it changes review behavior, so record three numbers per month and compare them against a baseline month before adoption. These are method definitions, not results from any deployment.

Metric | Definition | Direction that suggests the split works
---|---|---
Review latency by class | Median hours from draft to promotion |  `derivable` falls well below `interpretive`
Rework rate | Share of promotions that are edited within 14 days | Falling for `derivable`, flat elsewhere
Stale promissory pages | Count failing the window check on the scheduled run | Falling after the owner routing lands

A rising rework rate on `derivable` pages is the clearest signal that a page was misclassified. The remedy is to reclassify it as `interpretive` and accept human authorship of the reasoning, instead of adding more prompt instructions.

##  Limitations and who should skip this

The manifest is page-level, so a single page mixing a config table with a support commitment cannot be split automatically; in practice those cases should be separated into two pages. The class is self-declared, which means the gate enforces consistency rather than truth, and a determined author can mislabel a page without any tool noticing. The staleness check assumes `last_human_review` is updated honestly, so promotion must be the only path that writes that field in your process. Finally, nothing here validates the prose itself; it validates who is allowed to finish it.

Skip this approach if you are a single maintainer with a dozen pages, because the manifest becomes a second thing to maintain for no review savings. Skip it as well if your docs are generated entirely from code annotations, where the source of truth already implies the class. Teams without a designated docs owner should appoint one first, since a gate with no owner just produces failing builds.

If you do run a batch drafting pass on a free server, keep the promotion command as the only write path into `docs/` and let the manifest, not the model, decide what a page is allowed to be.
external.title: Draft Freely, Publish Narrowly: A Page Ownership Gate for Model-Written Docs
